parts.text:
1
What is a reasonable estimate of the volume of an adult person?
A
0.10 m3
B
0.50 m3
C
1.0 m3
D
2.0 m3

hints: Start from a typical adult mass of about $70 \text{ kg}$ rather than guessing volume directly.
Notice that people just float in water, so body density is close to $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Use $V = m / \rho$ with those numbers to get a volume in $\text{m}^3$ and see which listed value from $0.10 \text{ m}^3$ to $2.0 \text{ m}^3$ it matches.
walkthrough: Estimate the mass of an adult as $m \approx 70 \text{ kg}$.
Recall that the human body barely floats in water, so its density is $\rho \approx 1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$.
Use density $\rho = m / V$ rearranged to $V = m / \rho$.
Substitute with units: $V \approx 70 / 1000 = 0.07 \text{ m}^3$, so about $0.10 \text{ m}^3$ to one significant figure.
Values of $0.50 \text{ m}^3$ to $2.0 \text{ m}^3$ would mean $500 \text{ kg}$ to $2000 \text{ kg}$ at this density, which is not reasonable. This is option A

A.explanation: A mass of about $70 \text{ kg}$ at density near $1000 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ gives $V \approx 0.07 \text{ m}^3$, closest to $0.10 \text{ m}^3$.

B.explanation: At water density $0.50 \text{ m}^3$ would need a mass of about $500 \text{ kg}$, far too large for an adult.

C.explanation: A volume of $1.0 \text{ m}^3$ is a $1 \text{ m}$ cube and would imply a mass of about $1000 \text{ kg}$.

D.explanation: A volume of $2.0 \text{ m}^3$ would imply a mass of about $2000 \text{ kg}$, impossible for a person.
